content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have developed the National Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP), which is designed to provide structured lifestyle change programs aimed at delaying or preventing the onset of type 2 diabetes. Programs such as the Medicare Diabetes Prevention Program (MDPP) offer behavioral counseling services specifically targeted at individuals who are overweight and at high risk for developing diabetes. Eligibility for coverage under the MDPP requires a body mass index (BMI) of at least 25 kg/m², or 23 kg/m² for Asian Americans, ensuring that individuals at significant risk receive appropriate interventions. However, access to these programs remains a challenge for some individuals due to barriers such as geographic location and financial costs. Efforts to expand Medicare and Medicaid coverage, as well as the inclusion of registered dietitian nutritionists (RDNs) and community health workers, have been shown to enhance both the accessibility and effectiveness of these diabetes prevention programs.
